challengeFindings.title: A new labelled, chained or & edge in the adoption-order chart is silently dropped by adoptionArrows, and docPaths counts .bkit/templates/docs/x.md or docs/x.mdx as a prerequisite, so the chart and a starter's Fill these first line can disagree while the starter-shape tests stay green

A testing.md or deployments.md section whose first line is plain text but which quotes a Project slot or bkit practice marker further down passes 'marks every section slot or practice', and a slot section holding a nested practice marker skips the [e.g., table check, because sectionMarks and starterProblems use lines.some instead of the first non-blank line

A starter that carries the bkit-practice rules-box line but has no section marked bkit practice passes the 'rules box iff the starter holds one' check, because hasPractice scans the whole file and counts the rules-box line itself

An ASCII lane diagram drawn with │, ─, └, ┘, ├ or ► (or in an indented code block or a ~~~ fence) passes 'testing ... has no box-drawing diagram', because boxDrawingLines looks only for [▼▲┌┐] inside triple-backtick fences

tests.testName: adoptionArrows reads labelled, chained and grouped edges
docPaths ignores template paths and longer suffixes

challengeFindings.title: An adoption-chart edge into a subgraph id (for example `W3 --> W4` after the chart is split by wave, as the § Docs rule asks past about 15 nodes) or into an id with no `["..."]` label is read as a prerequisite of a made-up `docs/Wave 4.md` path, so no starter's Fill these first line is checked against it and no error is raised

A starter with the same `##` heading twice (for example an unmarked `## Environments` slot above a marked one) passes the slot-or-practice and `[e.g.,`-row checks, because sections() resets the Map entry on the second heading and silently drops every line of the first section
